Fees are in USD. Additional re-entry fee: +USD 25. Extension: USD 3/day (min 15 days). Late overstay fine: USD 5/day. All fees payable online via the portal.
 Gratis Visa - Free of Charge

The following applicants are exempt from paying visa fees:

Children Under 10

All nationalities except US citizens eligible for gratis visa (up to 30 days). Normal fees apply for 90-day visas.

SAARC Citizens

Free visa for up to 30 days, once per calendar year (January–December). Afghan nationals eligible on-arrival only with DoI recommendation.

Chinese Nationals

Eligible for gratis tourist visa for up to 150 days (≈5 months) per visa year.

NRN Card Holders

Non-Residential Nepalese (NRN) citizenship or card holders issued by Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Indian citizens do not require a visa to enter Nepal. Gratis visa applicants must still complete the online application process - no fee is charged upon submission.
 Visa on Arrival - Restrictions

Citizens of the following countries cannot obtain a Visa on Arrival at Nepal's immigration entry points. These applicants must apply in advance via a Nepalese Embassy or the online mission portal.

Nigeria
Ghana
Zimbabwe
Swaziland
Cameroon
Somalia
Liberia
Ethiopia
Iraq
Palestine
Afghanistan
Syria
All other passport holders may obtain a Visa on Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and other designated entry points. Follow the VoA counters upon arrival.
Restricted country nationals must apply via the Embassy Mission Portal before travelling.
 Visa Extension in Nepal

Tourist visas can be extended inside Nepal up to a combined maximum of 150 days per visa year (January–December). Extensions are processed by Department of Immigration offices in Kathmandu and Pokhara.

Diplomatic Visa

The diplomatic visa shall be issued to a person holding a diplomatic passport issued from any country and recommended from the concerned foreign diplomatic mission, to a person considered fit to be granted diplomatic privileges by Nepal Government, and the family members of such a person.

 The diplomatic visa is issued on the basis of reciprocity. Its term may be extended at a time or from time to time for the duration of the assignment in Nepal.
Who is Eligible?
Holders of a diplomatic passport issued from any country
Persons recommended by the concerned foreign diplomatic mission
Persons granted diplomatic privileges by Nepal Government
Family members of eligible diplomatic passport holders
Application Process

An application must be made in the format referred to in Appendix 1. However, if a request or recommendation accompanied by the details is made by a foreign diplomatic mission or a body authorised therefor, the application form is not required.

Tourist VISA Transit VISA Visitor VISA Close Family VISA Ni Vanuatu Decent VISA
Description
A tourist visa for Vanuatu is designed for short-term travelers with a genuine intention of visiting the country for tourism, leisure, or social visits. This visa comes with specific conditions, including a maximum stay of 120 days without the possibility of extension. Visa holders are not allowed to engage in commercial, employment, or business activities, and they must exit the country before the 120-day validity expires. Tourist visas can be obtained upon arrival for travelers from exempted countries or through a pre-approved application process for those from non-exempted countries.
Criteria
To be eligible for a tourist visa to Vanuatu, applicants must meet the following criteria:
Not being a prohibited immigrant.
Not being a person prevented by the Minister from entering Vanuatu.
Passing a character test.
Not suffering from contagious diseases or mental conditions that could pose a risk to the Vanuatu community’s health.
Providing security as required under the Immigration Act.
Having the financial means to support oneself and any dependents in Vanuatu.
Having a genuine intention of visiting and departing Vanuatu within 120 days.
Possessing a return ticket or satisfactory means of traveling from Vanuatu to another destination.
Obtaining written consent from parents or legal guardians if under 18 years of age.
Change Of Status
The tourist visa for Vanuatu does not allow for a change of status. Holders of this visa are strictly prohibited from engaging in commercial, employment, or business activities while in the country.
Fees
The visa application charge for non-exempted countries is 5,150 VUV. This fee is required when applying for the tourist visa. It’s important to note that visa fees and requirements may change over time, so applicants should verify the current fees and procedures through official government sources or the Vanuatu embassy or consulate before applying.
Validity
The tourist visa for Vanuatu is valid for a maximum period of 120 days. This visa does not allow for extensions, and the holder must depart the country before the 120-day period expires.
How To Apply
Applying for a tourist visa to Vanuatu depends on your home country’s status:
If you are from an exempted country, you can obtain a tourist visa upon arrival in Vanuatu, provided you meet the grant criteria.
If you are from a non-exempted country, you must apply for the visa in advance and obtain approval before traveling to Vanuatu.

Description
A transit visa for Vanuatu is intended for travelers who do not plan to leave the airport proclaimed area during a layover within the country and expect to stay for a maximum of 24 hours. If a traveler intends to exit the airport during their transit or stay for longer, they must apply for an appropriate visa, such as a tourist visa. For further information or inquiries, individuals can contact the Vanuatu immigration services via email at [email protected].
Criteria
To be eligible for a transit visa in Vanuatu, travelers must adhere to the following criteria:
Have a genuine intention to remain within the airport proclaimed area for a duration of no more than 24 hours.
Ensure that if they intend to leave the proclaimed area or stay longer in Vanuatu, they apply for the appropriate visa category, such as a tourist visa.
Change Of Status
A transit visa is specifically for travelers who do not plan to exit the airport proclaimed area during their layover in Vanuatu. It does not allow for a change of status or the extension of stay for purposes outside of transit. If a traveler intends to leave the airport or stay longer in Vanuatu, they must apply for the appropriate visa category, such as a tourist visa, that permits such activities.
Fees
The visa application charge for a transit visa in Vanuatu is 1,855 VUV. Travelers must ensure that this fee is paid when applying for the transit visa. Keep in mind that visa fees and requirements may change over time, so it is crucial to verify the current fees and procedures through official government sources or the Vanuatu embassy or consulate before applying for a transit visa.
Validity
A transit visa for Vanuatu is valid only for a short duration, allowing travelers to remain within the airport proclaimed area for up to 24 hours. It does not permit an extension of stay or exit from the airport area for other purposes.

Description
A visitor visa for Vanuatu is designed for individuals who are currently outside Vanuatu, are not exempt from visa requirements, and intend to visit Vanuatu for up to 30 days. This type of visa is suitable for various purposes, including tourism, visiting friends or family, attending meetings or conferences, and other short-term visits.
Criteria
To be eligible for a visitor visa in Vanuatu, applicants must meet the following criteria:
Be outside Vanuatu at the time of application.
Complete and sign the Visitor Application form, ensuring that all health and character questions are answered on the application form.
Pay the required visa application charge, which is 7,420 VUV.
Provide a certified copy of the bio-data page of a valid passport and all used pages of the passport (if in a proclaimed area, a valid passport is required).
Show evidence of a return ticket or proof of other arranged transport from Vanuatu within 30 days of arrival.
Demonstrate funds or income to support the applicant for the duration of the stay (at least 40,000 vatu per month) or provide evidence of support from family/friends in Vanuatu.
Present evidence of a genuine intention to depart Vanuatu within 30 days. This can include a letter from the employer confirming leave, a letter of invitation if visiting family or friends, or other relevant information. Supporting documents not in English, French, or Bislama must be translated into one of these languages.
If the applicant is under 18 years of age, both parents or legal guardians must provide consent to the grant of the visa.
If the applicant is under 18 years of age, not part of an organized tour, and won’t be accompanied by at least one parent or guardian in Vanuatu, an undertaking from a Vanuatu citizen or a visa holder in Vanuatu must be provided to ensure accommodation, food, and general welfare during the stay.
Change Of Status
Visitor visa holders must abide by specific conditions, including complying with all laws of Vanuatu, behaving in a manner that does not prejudice peace, good order, good government, or public morality in Vanuatu, refraining from paid employment or commercial business activities in Vanuatu, and promptly informing Vanuatu Immigration of any significant changes in personal or financial circumstances.
Fees
The visa application charge for a visitor visa in Vanuatu is 7,420 VUV. Ensure that this fee is paid when applying for the visa. Incomplete or partially complete applications will not be accepted.
Validity
A visitor visa for Vanuatu is valid for a maximum period of 30 days.

To be eligible for a Close Family Visa in Vanuatu, applicants must meet the
following criteria:
• The applicant may be in Vanuatu or outside Vanuatu at the time of his

• The applicant must be sponsored by:
▪ A Vanuatu citizen or
▪ A non-citizen who is residing in Vanuatu as the holder of a visa
which provides for secondary applicants
• The applicant must be the spouse or dependent child of the sponsor
• The Director must be satisfied that the sponsorship is acceptable
• If the applicant is sponsored by his or her spouse, the director must be

Change of status:
Close Family Visa of Vanuatu allows for multiple entry, is allowed to extend his
or her visa subject to prescribed conditions and also provides for secondary
applicant. The holders of this visa must not engage in any employment,
commercial or business activities and is not allowed to change his or her visa
status.
Fees:
When applying for Close Family visa in Vanuatu, applicants should be aware
of the following visa application fees:
• Adults: 61,800 Vatu
• Under 18 years of age: 5,150 Vatu
Validity:
Close Family Visa of Vanuatu is valid for a maximum period of 12 months.

To be eligible for a Ni Vanuatu Descent Visa in Vanuatu, applicants must meet

Vatu. Ensure that the fees are paid when applying for the visa. Incomplete or

Validity:
Ni Vanuatu Descent Visa for Vanuatu is valid for a maximum period of 12
months.

Carte d'Embarquement Électronique
Formulaire Digital d'Arrivée pour Haïti
Le formulaire iKat est là pour collecter des informations sur toutes les personnes entrant dans le pays.
Remplir le formulaire
Modifier le formulaire
Le formulaire électronique d'entrée et de sortie (iKat) est un outil qui permet aux voyageurs de fournir des informations aux préalables, 72h avant leur arrivée ou départ afin d'accélérer les formalités aux différents points d'entrée, y compris : les aéroports, les ports maritimes et les postes frontières terrestres.
En remplissant le formulaire iKat, les voyageurs fournissent des informations précises et actualisées sur leurs identités, leurs voyages et leurs santés, ce qui simplifie et améliore les procédures dans les dispositions des autorités afin de mieux préparer votre arrivée ou départ.
Le formulaire iKat comprend plusieurs sections, telles que : les informations personnelles, les détails du voyage, les informations sur le vol ou le transport terrestre, et les informations de douane. Les voyageurs sont tenus de remplir toutes les sections du formulaire avec des informations précises et véridiques.
Avantages
Permettre au voyageur de remplir le formulaire quelle que soit sa localisation.
Réduire les contacts et les échanges de documents avec les autorités.
Recevoir un traitement personnalisé et ajusté à vos besoins à votre arrivée.
Accéder aux services touristiques et étatiques durant votre séjour.
Foire aux Questions
Qu'est-ce que iKat ?
Ce formulaire doit être remplit par tous les voyageurs, Haïtiens et étrangers qui désirent entrer ou laisser Haïti.
Qui doit remplir le formulaire ?
Ce formulaire doit être rempli par tous les voyageurs, Haïtiens et étrangers qui désirent entrer ou laisser Haïti.
Que se passe-t-il si je ne le remplis pas avant le voyage ?
Chaque passager est averti qu’il doit obligatoirement remplir le formulaire 48 heures à l’avance. Au cas où vous ne l’auriez pas fait, vous devrez le remplir Avant de passer les différents points de contrôles, ce qui compliquera votre voyage.
À quoi sert le code QR que l’on obtient après avoir rempli le formulaire ?
Le code QR sera demandé aux voyageurs par les autorités sanitaires et douanières au moment de passer les points de contrôle. C’est ce code qui atteste que le formulaire a été correctement rempli.
Est-il important de conserver le code QR ?
Oui, ce code vous sera demandé à votre arrivée en Haïti par les autorités sanitaires et douanières.Il vous sera aussi demandé au moment de laisser le pays.
Pourquoi ce formulaire est-il si long ?
Ce formulaire unique, remplace les trois formulaires actuellement demandés : les informations personnelles, les informations de voyage, le formulaire de déclaration de douane et la déclaration sanitaire sur l’honneur du voyageur. Maintenant, toutes ces informations figurent sur un seul document.
Devrais-je remplir un autre document à mon arrivée en Haïti ?
Non, ce formulaire contient toutes les informations qui sont demandées aux voyageurs à leur entrée en Haïti et au moment de laisser le pays.
Si je voyage en famille, dois-je remplir un formulaire pour chaque membre de ma famille ?
Si vous voyagez en famille, vous devez remplir un formulaire pour chaque membre de la famille.
Dois-je aussi remplir un formulaire pour les enfants ?
Oui, vous devez aussi remplir un formulaire individuel avec toutes les informations demandées.
Peut-on présenter un code QR imprimé ?
Oui, on peut l’avoir imprimé ou sur son téléphone portable.
Jusqu'à quel moment peut-on remplir ce formulaire ?
Comme le formulaire papier actuel, on doit le remplir avant de passer les différents points de contrôle.
Que se passe-t-il si je ne le remplis pas avant le voyage ?
S’il vous faut apporter une modification quelconque aux données déjà envoyées au portail d’iKat, sélectionnez l’option ‘‘modifier le formulaire’’, saisissez le code du formulaire et le numéro de passeport, et faites vos modifications.
Dois-je remplir ce formulaire à chaque voyage ?
Oui, vous devrez remplir le formulaire à chaque voyage.

E-Visa
Nationals of USA and of other eligible countries can also apply for E-Visa under different categories (Tourist, Business, Ayush, Ayush Attendant, Medical, Medical Attendant, Student, Student-Dependent and Conference) at Government of India website:
https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/
The following may also be noted in this regard:
Visa applicants are cautioned against using any other website which may appear to represent the Government of India and only use the Government of India portal which is https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/tvoa.html
Passport used by the applicant should have at least six months validity from the date of arrival in India. The passport should have at least two blank pages for stamping by the Immigration Officer on arrival.
The applicant must travel on the passport on which e-Visa has been applied. Entry into India will be allowed on a new passport even if the e-Visa has been granted on the old passport. However, in such cases, the traveler must also carry the old passport on which the e-Visa has been granted.
E-Visa is not available to Diplomatic/Official Passport Holders or Laissez-passer travel document holders.
E-Visa is not available to individuals endorsed on Parent's/Spouse's Passport i.e. each individual should have a separate passport.
E-Visa is not available to International Travel Document Holders.
Applicants requiring help regarding e-Visa may call the 24X7 helpline number 011-24300666, +91-8278087808) or send an email to indian-evisa@gov.in for any queries.
The e-Visa facility is in addition to the existing Regular (Paper) Visa services being provided through Indian Embassy and Consulates.
Advisory: The applicant may note that the Embassy does not process e-visas and any enquiries in this regard will need to be made directly on the e-visa portal. Service of e-Visa involves a completely online application for which no facilitation is required by any intermediary / agent etc. Applicants are, therefore, advised to be cautious and for any clarification, please contact indian-evisa@gov.in.

Advisory for Canadian Nationals
e-Visa has 9 sub-categories viz. e-Tourist Visa(for 30 days/01 year/ 05 years), e-Business Visa, e-Medical Visa, e-Student Visa , e-Transit Visa , e-Film Visa,e-Miscellaneous Visa, e-Entry Visa and e-Production Investment Visa. Only two e-Medical Attendant Visas will be granted against one e- Medical Visa.
For e-Tourist and e-Business visa, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival.
For e-Medical and e-Medical Attendant, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival with a window of 120 days. Example: If you are applying on 1st Sept then applicant can select arrival date from 5th Sept to 2nd Jan
Sample eVisa application form is available on the tab near the bottom of eVisa main page.
Recent front facing photograph with white background and photo page of Passport containing personal details like name, date of birth, nationality, expiry date etc are to be uploaded mandatorily by the applicant. Additionally one more document depending upon the e-Visa type would also be required to be uploaded. The application is liable to be rejected if the uploaded documents and photograph are not clear / as per specification.
e-Visa fee is country/Territory specific. Bank transaction charges of 3% will be charged additionally on applicable e-Visa fees. The fee must be paid at least 4 days before the expected date of travel otherwise application will not be processed. To know the fee applicable on your Country/Territory please Click here (for e-Tourist Visa) and for other e-Visa Click here.
e-Visa fee once submitted is non-refundable as the fee is for processing of the application and is not dependent on either Grant or Rejection of Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA).
Applicant should carry a copy of Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) along with him/her at the time of travel. Please confirm that your ETA status is shown as 'GRANTED' on this website prior to commencement of your journey. Applicants can track the status of their application online by clicking VisaStatus
Biometric details of the applicant will be mandatorily captured at Immigration on arrival in India.
e-Visa is non-extendable, non-convertible & not valid for visiting Protected/Restricted and Cantonment Areas. If you intend to visit Protected/Restricted/Cantonment areas, you would require prior permission from the Civil Authority please visit here.
The e-Visa fee payment status updation may take up to 2 hours due to technical reasons/network delays. Before re-applying, the applicants are requested to wait for 2 hours for payment status updating, after final submission of the application form and payment of the fee. In cases, where e-Visa fee has been deducted but status is not updated, the applicants are advised to verify their payment status by clicking on 'Verify Payment/Pay Visa Fee' tab or by clicking on the link Verify Payment.
Nationals of Yellow Fever affected countries or travellers arriving from these countries must carry YELLOW FEVER VACCINATION CARD at the time of arrival in India, otherwise they may be quarantined for 6 days upon arrival in India. Please visit our Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare latest guidelines regarding yellow fever countries here.
You must travel on the Passport which you have applied for eVisa. Entry will be allowed into India on the new passport even if ETA has been issued on the old passport, however in such cases a traveler must carry the old passport on which ETA was issued

1. What is SBIePay?
SBIePay is the Payment Aggregator service of State Bank of India, India's Largest Bank and amongst top 50 Banks in the world, which provides bouquet of multiple payment options on a single page for the convenience of the customers.
2. What are the payment channels available for e-Visa?
SBIePay has facilitated the following channels on e-Visa platform:
Payment Gateway: It seamlessly processes Credit card and Debit Card transactions for all the cards issued internationally by Visa & MasterCard. SBIePay Payment gateway is enabled with BIN identifier which recognises the BIN online when a customer enters the no., which drastically improves the success percentage and reduces customer friction.
Paypal: SBIePay also facilitates e-Visa customers to make payment through widely popular and accepted Paypal channel.
3. Are transactions on SBIePay secure?
SBIePay is certified with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) ver 3.2, which is the latest version, and which further reinforces our promise of security and safety. The payment system fully supports 3DSecure - Verified by Visa and MasterCard Secure Code, wherever it is applicable. Further, SBIePay is secured using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption which ensures that payment information that travels over the Internet is always encrypted and cannot be viewed by unauthorised individuals.
4. Can International payments be processed?
Yes, SBIePay has enabled international card issued by MasterCard and VISA both with and without 3D Secure authentication.
5. How a customer/applicant can understand that payment has been made successfully?
The applicant enters necessary details on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/, and clicks on 'Pay Now'. The applicant is redirected to SBIePay payment page and is presented with payment options of either entering Card details (Payment Gateway) or Paypal.Applicant enters his card details and clicks "Proceed". Now, either of the below mentioned 2 scenarios will occur:
3 D Secure page of the Card Issuerwill be displayed, where applicant must enter 3D Secure Password/OTP.
Transaction is processed without 3D Secure page. After successful completion of transaction, the applicant is redirected on to the https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ with a successful receipt of payment.
6. How do I know that my Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction?
If an applicant is presented with a 3D Secure page prompting to enter a password/OTP, this means the Card issuing Bank participates in 3D Secure transaction. If the applicant's transaction is processed without directing to 3D secure page, he/she should contact the card issuing Bank for support.
7. What if a successful page on https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ is not shown after completing the transaction?
In an ideal scenario, once the transaction is processed, the applicant shall be presented with a payment successful page along with a reference number.
In some rare scenarios it may happen where the application is not shown Payment successful page post completion of transaction, which may be due to a drop in connectivity leading to non-receipt of success response. If the applicant does not receive any success message even after card account has been charged, a refund shall be initiated after due reconciliation process to the applicant's card account.
8. How are Refunds processed?
In rare case of transaction status unknown to the applicant, which is when the applicant has not received success response due to time out or connectivity issue and the account has been debited, we advise the customer not to attempt another transaction immediately and rather provide their Order no. on the e-Visa site after 30 minutes to check the status of the transaction. If the transaction status is showing "failed", then customer may attempt another transaction. Also, the debited amount shall be refunded to the applicant's card account after reconciliation process within seven (7) days of transaction.
9. What are the banking charges for e-Visa fee?
The banking charges for:
Payment Gateway Card transactions (both Debit or Credit Card): 3%* of the applicable e-Visa fee.
Paypal: 4%* of the applicable e-Visa fee.
*The charges are inclusive of any applicable taxes.
The breakup of transaction charges will be displayed on the Payment page for applicant's knowledge and to maintain transparency.

Contact No: +91-022-65361671
11. Can an applicant perform more than one transaction for same application number registered at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/?
An applicant can perform multiple times transactions for a single application ID, with a gap of minimum 25 minutes between each transaction. It is advisable that applicant may check the status of the transaction at e-Visa portal before attempting another transaction.
12. Can https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/ charge more than one time for an application ID?
An applicant shall be charged for only once for any successful transaction against an application ID. Any further debits shall be refunded back to the customer after due reconciliation, within seven (7) days of transactions.

Q1. Who is eligible for e-Visa Services?
Ans- The following are the eligibility conditions for availing e-Visa services-
i. Nationals of countries listed on the e-Visa website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ are eligible to apply for e-Visa Services.
ii. Foreigners whose sole objective for visiting India is
(a) Recreation and sightseeing
(b) Casual visit to meet friends and relatives
(c) Attending short term yoga programme or short term courses on local languages, music, dance, arts & crafts, cooking, medicine etc. which should not be a formal or structured course/programme
(courses not exceeding 6 months duration and not issuing a qualifying certificate/diploma etc. to the participants)
(d) Voluntary work of short duration (for a maximum period of one month, which do not involve any monetary payment or consideration of any kind in return)
(e) Medical treatment, including treatment under Indian systems of medicine
(f) As attendant to e-Medical visa holder
(g) Business purpose
(h) Attending a conference/ seminar/ workshop.
iii. Passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa and a re-entry permit, if that is required under the law of the country of nationality of the applicant.
The passport should have at least two blank pages for stamping by the Immigration Officer.
iv. The foreigner should have return ticket or onward journey ticket, with sufficient money to spend during his/her stay in India.
v. Foreigners of Pakistani origin or having Pakistani Passport are not eligible for e-Visa. Foreigners who are not Pakistani nationals, but whose parents or grandparents (either paternal or maternal) was born
in, or was permanently resident in Pakistan, are also not eligible for e-Visa. They may apply for regular Visa at Indian Mission.
vi. Not available to Diplomatic/Official Passport Holders or Laissez-passer/ international travel document holders.
vii. Not available to individuals endorsed on Parent's/Spouse's Passport i.e. each individual should have a separate passport.

Ans- For details regarding procedure for applying, please visit our website: https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/

Ans- No, https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ is only the official website to apply for the e-Visa Services.
Note - Services of e-Visa are completely online and no facilitation is required by any intermediary / travel agents etc. It is advised not to believe or fall in trap of any such unscrupulous elements who claim
speedy/express grant of e-Visa and charge money for it.
Do not share your personal information with any unauthorized website as it may lead to leakage of your personal data. Only visit the official website https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/ for e-Visa
service.
For any clarification, you may write us on our email id ' indian-evisa[at]gov[dot]in ' or contact us on (+91) 827808 7808 or +91 11 24300666.
Q4. Is there any fee other than the processing fee?
Ans- No, there is no fee other than the processing fee for e-Visa application and it is non-refundable. Please visit our website to know the fee applicable for your country as it is country-specific.
Q5. When should I apply?
Ans- (i) For e-Tourist Visa (01 year / 05 years), e-Business Visa, e-Medical, e-Medical Attendant and e-Conference visa, applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance
of the date of arrival. Such application can be made 120 days in advance from proposed date of travel.
(ii) For e-Tourist Visa (30 days) , applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival. Such application can be made 120 days in advance from
proposed date of travel.

application form.
Q7. When will my e-Visa be issued and how will I be informed about it?
Ans- You will be intimated about your Visa status (Granted or Rejected) on your email id provided by you in the e-Visa application.
Q8. Can I check the status of my e-Visa application?

Q9. What is the validity of e-Visa?
Ans- The validity of e-Visa would be according to the e-Visa service you have requested in the application form as -
For e-Tourist Visa (01 year / 05 years), the validity would be 365 days / 05 years from the date of grant of ETA with Multiple entries and Maximum stay in India during one Calender Year should not exceed 180 days.
For e-Tourist Visa (30 days), the validity would be 30 days from the date of your first arrival in India. Multiple entries will be granted within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport. Your first
arrival must be between the date of issue and expiry of ETA.
For e-Business Visa, the validity would be 365 days from the date of grant of ETA with Multiple entries and continuous stay during each visit which shall not exceed 180 days and no registration would be
required if stay is for a period of less than 180 days. However, if the intention is to stay for more than 180 days, then the foreigner shall get himself/herself registered with the FRRO/FRO concerned
(https://indianfrro.gov.in) within two weeks after the expiry of 180 days of his/her arrival in India.
For e-Conference Visa, the validity would be 30 days from the date of arrival in India with Multiple entry.
For e-Medical Visa, the validity would be 60 days from the date of first arrival in India and Multiple entry will be allowed within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport.
For e-Medical Attendant Visa, the validity would be 60 days from the date of first arrival in India and Multiple entry will be allowed within the e-Visa validity period stamped on your Passport.

About ETA-IL
Step by step
New: Quick & easy travel approval

Visitors from visa-exempt countries can apply for travel authorization through the ETA-IL system. Those who are eligible will be able to travel to Israel, and stay for up to 90 days or less.

Questions? Click here

Validity
2 Years

Or less

Duration
Up to 90 Days

Per visit

Cost
25 NIS

Application fee
(You cannot get a refund after you apply)

Your ETA-IL will stay valid for up to 2 years, or until your current passport expires – whichever comes first. If you obtain a new passport or change your name, gender or country of citizenship, you will be required to apply for a new travel authorization.

What can you do with an ETA-IL?
Enjoy Israel as a tourist
Doing Business
Travel for non-work and non-medical purposes
You must
Be eligible (check if you are eligible)
Be a citizen of an eligible country
Have a valid passport
ETA-IL Exemptions:
Foreign nationals with official Israeli documents
Travelers with a valid Israeli visa (B1, B3, B4, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5)
travelers holding a foreign passport who also has Israeli citizenship
Travel and official representatives
Crew members that appear on the Crew APIS
U.S military members holding CAC
Seamen with seamen book
Diplomats and passengers with official and service passports
You can apply for an ETA-IL if:
1
You are a citizen of a country that is exempt from visa to Israel
2
Your passport must be valid for at least three months from the date of your arrival in Israel
3
You plan to visit Israel for up to 90 days

Obtaining an ETA-IL does not constitute a guarantee of entry into Israel.

An Electronic Travel Authorization only allows you to reach the border-crossing into Israel, but does not grant you permission to enter or reside in Israel. When you arrive at the border-crossing, you will be checked by a border control officer, who may determine that you are not authorized to enter Israel.

Note: Israeli citizens or holders of an Israeli identity number do not need to apply for an ETA-IL

All Indonesia: Simplify Your Arrival
Admin Kantor Imigrasi Kelas I Non TPI Manokwari
 Berita Utama
 30 October 2025
 Hits: 2959
  

Setiap WNI maupun WNA yang masuk ke Indonesia kini wajib mengisi data melalui All Indonesia, aplikasi dan situs resmi yang menyederhanakan proses kedatangan. Layanan ini memadukan informasi imigrasi, bea cukai, kesehatan, hingga karantina, sehingga proses masuk menjadi lebih cepat, mudah, dan aman tanpa perlu menunggu lama.

Pernah merasa repot harus mengisi banyak formulir setelah tiba di Indonesia? Sekarang, semua jadi lebih simpel dengan aplikasi All Indonesia.

Tak perlu lagi mengisi formulir berulang kali saat mendarat. Cukup isi sekali sebelum tiba, dan seluruh proses kedatangan bisa langsung berjalan lebih cepat.

Satu-satunya aplikasi resmi yang memudahkan pelaporan kedatangan. Mulai dari keimigrasian, bea cukai, kesehatan, hingga karantina, semua terintegrasi dalam satu sistem berbasis mobile dan web.

Bagi penumpang dengan kebutuhan khusus seperti lansia, difabel, atau anak dibawah umur tanpa pendamping, pemeriksaan juga lebih cepat dan nyaman melalui Corridor Gate yang terhubung langsung dengan All Indonesia.

Dengan All Indonesia, satu aplikasi untuk semua proses kedatangan yang lebih mudah, cepat, dan aman.

Cara mengisi All Indonesia sangat mudah. Kamu hanya perlu mengakses allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id . Lalu, pilih Warga Negara Indonesia / Pengunjung Asing.
Kemudian isi Kartu Kedatangan:
- Isi data pribadi
- Masukkan detail perjalanan
- Pilih moda transportasi
- Centang deklarasi Bea Cukai/Custom
- Submit ➡ dapat QR Code ➡ tunjukkan pada petugas

Tariffs of consular fees of Turkmenistan
For registration and issuance of visas, the legislation of Turkmenistan provides for the following consular fees:
1) For single entry visas:
- up to 10 days - 20 US dollars;
- up to 20 days - 30 USD;
- up to 1 month - 40 USD;
- for each subsequent month - 30 US dollars.
2) For multiple entry visas:
- up to 1 month - 60 US dollars;
- for each subsequent month - 40 US dollars.
3) For transit visas:
- single up to 5 days - 20 US dollars;
- double up to 5 days each time - 40 USD.
4) For the issuance of visas at the international airport of Ashgabat, an additional charge is 50 US dollars.
When issuing visas, a fee is also charged to reimburse the actual costs associated with issuing visas. The amount of such fees depends on the place where visas are issued (regardless of the nationality of the applicant).
Consular actions are carried out within 10 calendar days from the moment the documents are received by the institution that performs them. For urgent consular activities within 3 working days, as well as for consular activities outside working hours, weekends and holidays, the fee rates increase by 100 percent.
Note: For citizens of states with which there are relevant bilateral agreements and understanding, a different procedure for issuing entry visas to Turkmenistan may be provided.

At the Border
A key function of the Migration Service is providing border control services to assess the identity and intent of travelers seeking to enter and depart the country.
Conditions applicable to entry
To enter the national territory all travellers must present themselves for immigration clearance at an official point of entry into Timor-Leste.
Foreigners must also satisfy the following basic requirements before they can be considered for entry:
Must hold a valid travel document (Passport, Laissez Passer, Seaman’s Passport or others), which if entering for tourism or transit that is valid for at least six months;
Must be of good character and health;
Must not have any outstanding fines under the Law on Migration & Asylum;
Must not be subject to a ban on re-entry under the Law on Migration & Asylum;
Must hold a valid visa, permit, authorization, or be eligible for a visa on arrival or entry via a visa exemption;
Have access to funds and accommodation sufficient for sustenance whilst in the country, regardless of the visa, permit, or visa exemption used to enter. In the case of entrants on a Tourist, Transit, or Business Class 1 visa, unless sponsored by family or other contact in the country, the funds required are
US$100 for each entry, and
US$50 for each day’s stay in the country.
Note: If you are seeking a Tourist or Transit visa on arrival, the visa fee must be paid in US$ cash. EFTPOS & credit card facilities are not available, and ATM machines and currency exchange may not be available, so please ensure you have the correct amount in US$ cash when you arrive.
See

Arrival and Departure Declarations
All travelers are required to complete and submit an official declaration online prior to entry or departure. This declaration is managed and collected via the Customs Authority Trade Single Window, and satisfies the requirements of the Migration Service, the Customs Authority, the National Directorate of Quarantine and Biosecurity (NDQB), the Ministry of Health, and the Central Bank of Timor-Leste.
It can be submitted up to three days before travel. It will save time if this is completed well before your arrival or departure. Keep a screenshot of the QR code or a printout of the PDF you get from the system once you complete the declaration and show this to border officials on arrival.
It is an official declaration, and penalties apply for any false or misleading declaration in accordance with the legislation of the respective agency.
See: Traveler declaration here.
Border Systems
The Migration Service operates a modern border management system which inspects all aspects of travel documents, and which collects personal identity and biometric data as permitted and required by the Law on Migration & Asylum (11/2017).
This information is protected by law, but may be used to identify travelers, verify the status of foreign nationals in the country, and to aid in national law enforcement and intelligence activity as mandated and regulated by law. Information may also be used to validate traveler identity and intent by querying other national and international databases.

Frequently Asked Questions
General conditions to enter the country+
To enter in national territory all travellers must present themselves for immigration clearance at an official point of entry into Timor-Leste.
Foreigners must also satisfy the following basic requirements before they can be considered for entry:
Must hold a valid travel document (Passport, Laissez Passer, Seaman Passport or others) that is valid for at least six months;
Must be of good character and health;
Must not have any outstanding fines under the Law on Migration & Asylum;
Must hold a valid visa, permit, authorization, or be eligible for a visa on arrival or entry via a visa exemption;
Have access to funds and accommodation sufficient for sustenance whilst in the country, regardless of the visa, permit, or visa exemption used to enter. In the case of entrants on a Tourist, Transit, or Business Class 1 visa, unless sponsored by family or other contact in the country, the funds required are
US$100 for each entry, and
US$50 for each day’s stay in the country.
See also: At the Border.
I want to travel to Timor-Leste as a tourist. Do I need a visa before I travel?+
Travellers of all nationalities, except for nationalities subject to separate a Visa waiver (exemption) arrangements, may apply for, and if they satisfy the criteria for grant, obtain a Tourist Visa on arrival. Tourist Visas on arrival are valid for 30 days stay, and can be extended once with same period. They allow single entry except where the applicant demonstrates they are travelling to Oecusse-Ambeno, in which multiple entries may be authorised.
See: Tourist Visa
See: Visa Exemptions
See: Contact Us
My passport expires soon. Can I still use it to travel to Timor-Leste?+
All foreigners seeking to enter Timor Leste are required to have a travel document (Passport, Laissez Passer, Seaman Passport) which is valid for more than six months on the date of entry, except in cases of re-entry of a resident or or holder of a special stay authorization or long-stay visa, and only if there are a diplomatic representation of the country of his nationality accredited in Timor-Leste, that is able to issue a new travel document.
I want to stay longer in the country. How do I do this?+
If eligible, apply for an extension at the headquarters of the Migration Service in Vila Verde, Dili.
Don’t wait until your current visa expires. Apply at least 15 days before the expiry date, with a complete and signed application form, attaching all the required documents.
See: Contact Us
See: Visas and Permits
Can I work on a Tourist Visa or Tourist Visa exemption?+
No. The Tourist visa is for tourism, and those who enter on a visa exemption for tourism have a similar stay condition. This form of entry and stay does not permit work as an employee. Those wishing to visit Timor Leste on business (e.g., to explore business opportunities, conduct negotiations etc.), may enter and stay for this purpose on a Business Visa Class I or Class II. Persons wishing to work in Timor Leste should apply for the appropriate Work Visa or Visa to establish residence to perform professional activities or a Special Stay Authorization.
See: Visas and Permits
I work for the UN or a UN agency in Timor-Leste. Do I need a visa?+
Diplomats and United Nations staff officially accredited to Timor-Leste are exempted from the requirement to hold a visa on their first arrival and upon issuance of their Diplomatc Identity Card after arrival, they are further exempted from the requirement to obtain any visa or resident permit for the duration of their accredited stay.
All holders of a United Nations Laissez-Passer (UNLP) or INTERPOL Travel Document (ITD) may enter Timor-Leste without a valid visa for up to 90 days. Note that those who are not officially accredited with the Diplomatic Identity card after arrival must obtain the relevant Special Stay Authorization or other appropriate visa if they wish to stay beyond this period.
I have overstayed my visa. Will there be a penalty?+
Yes. You should contact us immediately to regularize your status as soon as possible, or depart the country immediately. Do not let the situation wait longer than necessary. Article 141 of the Law on Migration and Asylum (11/2017) provides the following fines per person for those who have overstayed their visa in Timor-Leste:
US$ 150 to US$ 230, if the overstay period does not exceed 30 days;
US$ 230 to US$ 350, if the overstay period exceeds 30 days, but is less than 90 days;
US$ 350 to US$ 580, if the overstay period exceeds 90 days.
In accordance with Article 150 of the Law on Migration and Asylum (11/2017), overstayers will be issued a fine notice, which allows them to pay the minimum amount or appeal the fine within 10 calendar days.
Important Note :
Fines notices may be issued upon departure from the country, although having overstayed will not prevent departure.
Re-entry to the country, visa extensions or further visa grants cannot be authorized without proof of payment of any applicable fine for overstay.
See: Contact Us
I have become aware of a case of human trafficking or possible breaches of immigration law. Where do I report this?+
See: Irregular Migration.
I am the holder of a Schengen area passport. Do I need to apply for a Visa on arrival or before I travel if I am travelling as a tourist?+
No. According to the terms of a bilateral agreement between Timor-Leste and the European Union, Schengen area nationals of good health and character who present a Schengen Member State passport on arrival and who seek to enter for tourism are exempted from having to obtain Tourist visa on arrival.
You may stay for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period.
The stay period may be extended up to a further 90 days after arrival on application to the Migration Service, where that further stay is justified on exceptional grounds.
Note: This does not apply to citizens of Ireland and the United Kingdom.
See: Visa Exemptions
I was granted a Special Stay Authorization. Are my dependents eligible for the same Authorization?+
No. Your dependent/s should apply for a Temporary Stay Visa. The validity of the temporary stay visa of your dependant is the same as the validity of your Special Stay Authorization.
See: Temporary Stay Visa.
I am a Timorese citizen and my spouse is a foreign citizen. We married very recently. Can they apply for the Temporary Resident Permit?+
If they are located in the national territory, you should apply for family reunification pursuant to Article 70(1)(a) and and Article 59(c) of the Law on Migration & Asylum (11/2017), which provides that the spouse of a national citizen may be granted a Temporary Resident permit.
See: Temporary Resident Permit

Tourist Visa
The tourist visa is intended for foreigners who wish to travel to the country for the purpose of tourism. It is valid for a single entry, thirty days stay and may be extended once for the same period. In the case of travellers to Oecussi, multiple entries may be allowed where this is made known to the visa processing officer. Foreign citizens who hold a tourist visa are not allowed to exercise any professional activity in the country.
How and where to apply+
The visa may be applied for and obtained on arrival where the criteria for the visa are satisfied. This may be done at all official border posts, air, land, or sea, which are open for foreign nationals and which have a presence of the Migration Service.
See: Details of relevant border control posts here.
Note: foreigners who are subject to separate visa waiver or visa exemption arrangements do not need to apply for a Tourist Visa on arrival.
See: Visa exemptions.
For foreigners who have previously been refused entry, or removed or excluded from the country, or those who have outstanding fine amounts, the visa must be applied for and obtained prior to seeking entry to the national territory at an official border control point.
See: Overseas offices here.
Criteria+
The person applying for the visa must satisfy the decision-maker that:
They intend a genuine visit for tourism or to visit friends and family
They will not engage in employment or professional activity
Have complied with conditions of any previous visas or visa exemptions
They will comply with any other visa decisions, including stay period.
Are of good character and health.
Applicants must also be able to demonstrate they have suffient funds to support themselves during they stay in the country. Article 15 of the Law on Migration & Asylum provides this amount is:
US$100 dollars for each entry into national territory;
US$50 dollars for each day of stay in national territory.
This may be waived upon presentation of a term of responsibility (sponsorship) guaranteeing food and accommodation during the stay of the foreigner, namely:
a national citizen;
a holder of residence permit;
a holder of a diplomatic corps or consular card;
Temporary stay visa holder for specialised activity development;
a holder of a work visa;
Business visa holder;
holder of a residence visa;
a holder of a Special Stay Authorisation; or a
Registered corporate body in Timor-Leste.
Documentary requirements+
Where the visa is applied for on arrival, the applicant must present:
An acceptable travel document, valid for at least 6 months at the date of entry
A completed arrival declaration
If requested, evidence of sufficient funds to support stay in the country
If requested, evidence of acccomodation arrangements
If requested, evidence of departure arrangements such as an onwards transportation ticket or booking.
Where the visa is applied for prior to arrival at an Embassy or Consulate of Timor-Leste abroad:
A completed and signed application form, located here.
An acceptable travel document and copy, which will be valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry
Colour photograph (3x4cm) on plain background
Evidence of sufficient funds to support stay in the country or family sponsorship, form located here.
Evidence of acccomodation arrangements, or family sponsorship.
Evidence of departure arrangements such as an onwards transportation ticket or booking.
Other evidence justifying the grant of the visa if applicable.
Fee+
The fee is US$30, paid in US$ cash
Conditions+
Conditions applicable to the visa are:
Stay period 30 days
Holder may not undertake professional activity or employment, paid or unpaid
Single entry, unless the applicant informs the issuing officer that they intend to travel to Oecussi, in which case, multiple entry may be granted.
May be extended once only after entry, unless exceptional circumstances apply.
Extension+
In normal circumstances, the Tourist Visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days.
Form: See forms here.
Fee: US$40
Place of Application: In person at the Migration Service Headquarters in Dili.
Processing time: Up to 15 days.
Note: Where applications for extension are lodged more than 15 days prior to the current visa expiry, the counting of the validity of that visa is suspended. Where an extension application is lodged with less than 15 days remaining validity on the current visa, the counting of that validity is not suspended.
Further extensions are generally not permitted unless exceptional circumstances apply, such as for serious medical or humanitarian reasons, as well as genuine transportation issues which are not caused by the person concerned.

Visa exemptions
All foreign nationals seeking to enter and stay in the country require some form of authority to do so. Whilst this will often take the form of a visa, permit, or special stay authorization, some individuals are exempted from the requirement to hold a visa, and may also be exempted from the need to hold a resident permit to remain in the country.
Schengen Area Citizens+
On 26 May 2015 the European Union (EU) and Timor-Leste signed a short-stay visa waiver agreement.
The new visa regime provides for visa-free travel for Schengen Area citizens when travelling to the territory of Timor-Leste for a period of stay of 90 days in any 180-day period.
In order to benefit from visa-free travel, citizens from the EU and Timor-Leste must be in possession of a valid ordinary, diplomatic, service/official or special passport. Visa-free travel applies to all categories of persons and for any kind of purposes of travel (for instance tourism, cultural visits, scientific activities, family visits, business etc.), except to persons travelling for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity.
This includes the following States:
Austria
Belgium
Croatia
Cyprus
Czech Republic
Denmark
Estonia
Finland
France
Germany
Greece
Hungary
Italy
Latvia
Lithuania
Luxembourg
Malta
Netherlands
Poland
Portugal
Romania
Slovakia
Slovenia
Spain
Sweden
and the non-EU Schengen states:
Iceland
Liechtenstein
Norway
Switzerland
Note: Citizens of the United Kingdom and Ireland are NOT included in this arrangement.
See: the agreement text here.
ASEAN Citizens+
Citizens of the following ASEAN member States, holding passport of that State valid for 6 months past the entry date are visa exempt for stays of up to 30 days for tourism purposes:
Indonesia
Malaysia
Singapore
Thailand
Further agreements are being sought with remaining ASEAN member States, and this list will be updated accordingly.
Other bilateral agreements+
Several agreements are being negotiated but are not yet implemented. This section will be updated as these agreements are finalised.
Accredited Diplomats & UN Staff+
Diplomats and United Nations staff officially accredited to Timor-Leste are exempted from a visa on their first arrival and upon issuance of their Diplomatic Identity Card after arrival, they are exempted from the requirement to obtain any visa or resident permit for the duration of their accredited stay.
All holders of a United Nations Laissez-Passer (UNLP) or INTERPOL Travel Document (ITD) may enter Timor-Leste without a valid visa for up to 90 days. Note that those who are not officially accredited with the Diplomatic Identity card after arrival must obtain the relevant Special Stay Authorization or other appropriate visa if they wish to stay beyond this period.
Bearers of Diplomatic & Official or Service Passports+
All travelers holding a diplomatic, official or service passport may enter Timor-Leste on their first entry without visa for up to 90 days.
All holders of a United Nations Laissez-Passer (UNLP) or INTERPOL Travel Document (ITD) may enter Timor-Leste on their first entry without a valid visa for up to 90 days.

Visa de séjour
Visa de séjour
Ce type de visa est délivré aux personnes désirant prolonger leurs séjours au Burundi..
Il est d’une validité de 5 jours à 1 mois renouvelable. Il est délivré au Commissariat Général des Migrations. Il est payable de 10 $ tous les 5 jours pour un séjour inferieur ou égal à 25 jours pour un étranger dont le séjour d’un mois a expiré. Au delà de cette période, le paiement est de 70 $ par mois..
Le Burundais détenteur d’un passeport burundais et étranger et dont le visa d’entrée a expiré bénéficie d’un visa de séjour de 5 derniers jours moyennant paiement de 10 $, sur présentation de sa carte nationale d’identité..
Tarif: 10 $ tous les 5 jours pour un séjour inferieur ou égal à 25 jours
Validité: Maximum 25 jrs
Octroyé au CGM

Visa Etudiant
Visa Etudiant EAC
Le visa d’étude est délivré gratuitement aux élèves et étudiants ressortissant des pays membres de la Communauté de l’Afrique de l’Est qui s’inscrivent dans les écoles et universités du Burundi.
Tarif - Gratuit
Validité - 12 mois
Octroyé au CGM ou à tout point d’entrée
Visa Etudiant RDC
Ce visa est délivré aux étudiants ressortissants de la République Démocratique du Congo moyennant payement de vingt-cinq dollars américains par an. Il est apposé dans un passeport ou dans un laissez-passer tenant lieu de passeport valide d’au moins six mois.
Les élèves et étudiants ressortissants d’autres pays sont soit soumis aux accords spécifiques signés entre le Burundi et leurs pays, soit soumis au régime juridique régissant les autres étrangers en matière d’obtention de visas.
Tarif - 25 USD
Validité - Expire le 31 Décembre de l'année
Octroyé au CGM

Visa de séjour
Ce type de visa est délivré aux personnes désirant prolonger leurs séjours au Burundi..
Il est d’une validité de 5 jours à 1 mois renouvelable. Il est délivré au Commissariat Général des Migrations. Il est payable de 10 $ tous les 5 jours pour un séjour inferieur ou égal à 25 jours pour un étranger dont le séjour d’un mois a expiré. Au delà de cette période, le paiement est de 70 $ par mois..
Le Burundais détenteur d’un passeport burundais et étranger et dont le visa d’entrée a expiré bénéficie d’un visa de séjour de 5 derniers jours moyennant paiement de 10 $, sur présentation de sa carte nationale d’identité..
Tarif: 10 $ tous les 5 jours pour un séjour inferieur ou égal à 25 jours
Validité: Maximum 25 jrs

Visa d'établissement
Le demandeur d’un visa d’établissement de deux ans doit remplir les conditions qui suivent:
Payer cinq cent dollars américains;
Avoir résidé au moins 6 mois au Burundi;
Déposer une caution en compte bloqué de mille cinq cent dollars américains pour lui-même ou cinq mille dollars américains pour une famille, dans une banque agréée au Burundi et précisée par l’autorité compétente. Les enfants mineurs reçoivent gratuitement une copie conforme du visa de l’un des parents tandis que les enfants majeurs paient leurs visas et constituent leurs propres cautions;
Déposer en lieu et place d’une caution bancaire, une lettre de garantie émanant d’une institution ou organisation nationale ou internationale établie ou représentée au Burundi.
La caution est restituée ou la garantie levée lorsque l’étranger quitte définitivement le Burundi.
Fermer
Visa de résident permanent
Le visa de résident permanent peut être accordé à un étranger remplissant l’une des conditions qui suivent:
Avoir résidé pendant au moins 10 ans sans interruption au Burundi et prouvé qu’il a des investissements à son actif dans le pays; avoir résidé au moins 6 mois au Burundi;
Avoir résidé pendant au moins six mois au Burundi;
Avoir fait des investissements ayant un apport important dans l’économie du Burundi et créé de l’emploi durable en faveur des nationaux;
Etre mariée à un burundais pour une femme étrangère;
Contracter mariage avec une femme burundaise pendant au moins cinq ans et posséder sa propriété immobilière résidence au Burundi;
Le visa résident permanent est donné automatiquement à toute personne détentrice de l’ancien visa indéterminé moyennant payement de mille deux cent dollars américains.
La déchéance du visa de résident permanent accordé à un étranger peut être décidée si le détenteur:
Ne réunit plus les conditions qui ont motivé l’octroi de ce visa;
Est condamné à une peine de servitude pénale principale de plus de six mois;
Présente un comportement de nature à compromettre l’ordre public.
La décision d’accorder ou de retirer le visa de résident permanent est prise par le Ministre ayant la sécurité publique dans ses attributions sur avis motivé de la Commission Consultative pour Etrangers

Vistos de Entrada
Os vistos de entrada para a República de Moçambique podem ser obtidos nas Missões Diplomáticas e Consulares da República de Moçambique no estrangeiro, nos postos fronteiriços autorizados para o efeito, nos Serviços de Migração e no Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros e Cooperação.
O visto de entrada pode ser individual ou colectivo, simples ou múltiplo. O visto pode revestir qualquer das seguintes modalidades:
a) visto diplomático;
b) visto de cortesia;
c) visto oficial;
d) visto de residência;
e) visto turístico;
f) visto de trânsito;
g) visto de visita;
h) visto de negócios;
i) visto de estudante.
A entrada no país deve ser feita pelos postos fronteiriços oficialmente estabelecidos para o efeito. No momento da entrada, o cidadão estrangeiro está sujeito aos procedimentos migratórios das autoridades competentes, de entre outros previstos na lei.
É exigido para a entrada no território nacional, qualquer dos seguintes documentos:
a) Passaporte ou documento equiparado valido para o país e visto de entrada emitido pelas autoridades moçambicanas competentes, igualmente válidos;
b) Outros documentos estabelecidos em convenções ou acordos internacionais a que Moçambique se encontre vinculado.
Países com os quais Moçambique assinou acordos de supressão de vistos:
1. Isenção de VISTO em Todo o Tipo de Passaporte:
África do Sul, Botswana, Malawi, Mauricias, Swazilândia, Tanzânia, Zâmbia e Zimbabwe.
2. Inseção de VISTO em Passaporte Diplomático e de Serviço
a) Países da CPLP; e
b) Cuba.

Border Services
Meeting us at the borders
Any aircraft or vessel departing or arriving at any regulated port shall be attended by Immigration officers for travel document screening on the spot. The process employs the first-come-first-serve principle using the queuing system. Signs have been placed above the Immigration counters for public direction.
We are willing to give special treatment to:
Old age passengers
Mothers with babies
Medical and Disabilities
Members of Diplomatic missions
Special Ministerial cases
An officer will be available to provide assistance to passengers. Arrival and Declaration Cards will also be provided either by Airline/Shipping Agent or by Immigration Officers at Arrival Booths.
Vessel Clearance
The operator of every ship and aircraft about to arrive in or arriving in Samoa from another country shall deliver to the Officer on duty at such port or airport, as the case may require, prior to the ship's/aircraft's arrival. The Minister may require a list of all persons on the ship or aircraft, including but not limited to
Complete name
Date of birth
Nationality
Passport or other travel document number
Foreign nationals who do not hold a valid Temporary Resident Permit or Samoan Citizenship will be issued with a free 90 days Visitors Permit upon arrival. But grant of a Visitors permit is subject to our entry requirements, i.e the passenger must:
Have a return or onward ticket
Possess a passport valid for a minimum of 6 months after the intended date of departure from Samoa.
Have a valid visa or permit for entry into the country to which they will travel from Samoa.
State their accommodation arrangements, be it holiday accommodation such as a hotel or resort, or with family or friends (specifically the village and family name)
Have documented evidence of sufficient funds for self-support (typically a copy of a bank statement)
Have no record or deportation from other countries
Have no health problems that would pose a risk to Samoa
Have no history of criminal charges resulting in a minimum of one year of sentencing; and
Not be on any alert or warning lists
Other Field Duties
On matters relating to overstaying and illegal entries, inspections and investigations are conducted in residential addresses and boarding houses for the purposes of:
Updating office records
Follow up public compliance
The Minister may authorize in writing the Officers to enter, providing their identification to ensure lawful actions.

Samoa Immigration
Permit Services
By legislation, we service four types of entry permits: Visitor, Temporary Resident, Permanent Resident, and Ministerial.
Visitors
Visitors to Samoa can apply for a 90-day Visitor Permit on arrival using the arrival card. Travelers must have:
a passport valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended stay
confirmed onward tickets (Return Ticket)
visas for the next country of destination
sufficient funds to support themselves (while in Samoa)
confirmed residential contact address
Work is not permitted on a Visitor Permit. Visitors who are in Samoa and wish to apply for a further period of stay as a visitor should use the temporary residence form. A Business Visitor Permit is for persons normally employed and paid offshore who are visiting Samoa for a short visit, to visit a branch of their company, to conduct business negotiations with a Samoan company or to attend a business conference.
For other business activity in Samoa, a Temporary Resident Permit is required.
Application for further extension of your 90-day Visitor’s permit:
To apply for this extension, you must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Attach a photocopy of onward ticket out of Samoa
Provide evidence of sufficient funds to support your extended stay
Provide details of accommodation arrangements
Temporary Residence Information
Temporary Residence in Samoa can be issued for the following purposes:
Business and Investment
Employment
Study
Academic Research
Cultural and Religious purposes
Family Support or Reunion
Temporary Resident Permit for conduct of business or invest in Samoa:
Before applying for a Temporary Resident permit for business, investors need:
An Investment Certificate from Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
A Business License from Ministry for Revenue, and
Company Registration confirmation from Ministry of Justice & Courts Administration
With these prerequisite documents, investors also need to submit the following:
Completed application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Medical and Police reports (MPMC102, MPMC103)
Temporary Resident Permit for Employment:
To apply for temporary residence for Employment purposes, applicants must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Attach a completed Employer Sponsorship form (MPMC101)
Attach Medical and Police reports (MPMC102, MPMC103)
Enclose originals or certified copies of qualifications, or any supporting reference/documents
(A copy of the permit application will be provided to the Ministry of Commerce, Industry & Labour who will recommend if employment of a non-citizen is in the best interests of Samoa.)
Temporary Resident Permit for Study in Samoa:
To apply for temporary residence for Study purposes, applicants must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Attach a confirmation letter of enrollment from the relevant Educational institution; for Medical students, the confirmation letter must be provided by the Samoa Ministry of Health
Provide evidence of funds to support yourself for the duration of your stay
Provide a letter confirming details of award if studying under a scholarship, or evidence of accommodation if studying as a private student
Temporary Resident Permit for academic or scientific research in Samoa:
To apply for temporary residence for academic or scientific research purposes, applicants must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Provide a letter from your sponsoring academic institution to support your research
Provide a letter from any academic institution in Samoa supporting your research
Provide evidence of funds to support yourself while in Samoa
Provide evidence of your travel out of Samoa
Attach Medical and Police reports (MPMC102, MPMC103)
Your entry permit MUST be approved and granted before travel to Samoa.
Temporary Resident Permit for Cultural or Religious Purposes:
To apply for temporary residence for cultural or religious purposes, applicants must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Provide a confirmation letter from organizers of the event
Provide a letter from hosts indicating accommodation arrangements
Provide evidence of funds to support yourself for the duration of your stay
Temporary Resident Permit for Family Reunion or Family Support:
To apply for temporary residence for family reunion or family support purposes, applicants must:
Complete the application form for temporary residence (MPMC100)
Provide a confirmation letter from organizers of the event
Provide a letter from hosts indicating accommodation arrangements
Provide evidence of funds to support yourself for the duration of your stay
Attach Medical and Police reports (MPMC102, MPMC103)
MEDICAL REPORTS
A medical report is required for ALL persons intending to stay for 1 year or more (for those over 16 years of age).
A separate report is needed for each individual traveling to Samoa.
POLICE REPORTS
A police report is required for ALL persons over 18 years intending to stay for 1 year or more. It should include police reports from authorities of every country you have lived in for more than 1 year in the last 5 years.
Note on Employment:
It is an offence for a non-citizen to undertake employment in Samoa unless their Employment Permit specifically authorizes such employment.
Where a Temporary Resident Permit for Employment Purposes is granted, the holder is permitted to work for the employer nominated in the application. If this employment ceases for any reason, the Permit is subject to cancellation and the person must leave the country or apply for a new permit to remain in Samoa.
Visitors, Academic Researchers, Cultural and Religious personnel permit holders are not permitted to work in Samoa.
Students may work part time, if authorized. Dependents of permit holders may seek authority to undertake employment in Samoa during the validity period of the principal applicant’s permit.

Request an NZeTA
Use this page to check the requirements for an NZeTA (New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority), submit your request, and pay your International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL).
Mobile app

The fastest and cheapest way to request an NZeTA

Download now
You can scan your passport and payment card using the NZeTA app, instead of entering your details manually.
Requests made through the NZeTA app only cost NZD $17 (plus the IVL).
You will need
a valid passport that you will use to travel to New Zealand
a credit card or debit card (Visa or Mastercard) to pay
an email address to contact you
a photo of your face, or a device like a mobile phone that can take one
Cost
NZD $23 for NZeTA, if applying on the web, or NZD $17 for NZeTA, if applying on the mobile app.
NZD $100 for the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL)

The IVL helps pay for tourism infrastructure and conservation in New Zealand. You pay the IVL at the same time as your NZeTA.

Read more about the International Visitor Levy

Processing time

Most NZeTA requests are processed within 72 hours. Complex NZeTA requests may take longer. Apply early and make sure your details match your passport.

An approved NZeTA is valid for 2 years.

Read why some applications are processed faster than others

Privacy and biometric information

Your photo will be collected and used as biometric information to establish a record of your identity, verify your identity, and assist in making a decision on your NZeTA request.

Check our privacy statement and collecting and using biometric information pages for more about how we manage your privacy and handle biometric information. You can also learn about your rights, including access to information, correction of information, and complaints, including complaints to the Privacy Commissioner. Our NZeTA Terms of Use page also has important information.

Visas and citizenship
Welcome to the website of the Department of Home Affairs at the Australian Embassy in the Philippines. Home Affairs’ main webpage can be accessed at: http://www.homeaffairs.gov.au
Latest News / Important Notices
For the latest immigration and citizenship news, see News archive.
Business visitor visa (subclass 600) - 5 year validity
The Australian Government has announced improved visa access to Australia.
Business Visitor visa (subclass 600) validity will be extended up to five years.
These measures reaffirm Australia’s commitment to the ASEAN region by improving access and enabling closer economic collaboration.
For further information about the Business Visitor visa (subclass 600) visit Visitor visa (subclass 600) Business Visitor stream (homeaffairs.gov.au)
These changes came into effect on 01 April 2024.
For more information about Home Affairs, including immigration and citizenship, visit our website: www.homeaffairs.gov.au
Applying for an Australian visa from the Philippines
The Department of Home Affairs encourages visa applicants to Check twice, submit once! Please check out the video to ‘Get it right the first time for a faster visa process’
The Department of Home Affairs’ visa finder can assist you to identify the correct visa for your travel to Australia. So that we can process your application as quickly as possible for you, please ensure that you:
Read all the available information and instructions on the front of the application form and our website
Complete all the required details in the application form
Use our checklists to ensure you include all the required documentation
Make your appointment to have your biometrics collected as soon as you receive the request letter
All visa applications for Australia are required to be lodged through ImmiAccount. No paper applications are accepted.
Further information regarding ImmiAccount is available on the http://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/ website.
Visa Application Charges from 1 July 2023
From 1 July 2023 only Australian dollars will be accepted for Visa Application Charges, please see Visa pricing estimator (homeaffairs.gov.au).
ImmiAccount
Biometrics
Visa applicants in the Philippines must complete biometric (face photograph and fingerprint scan) collection for each application lodged, irrespective of their nationality, unless they are excluded or exempt from the biometric program.
Biometrics are collected through a quick and easy process that captures a photograph of your face and a 10-digit electronic fingerprint. Applicants will be required to provide their biometrics each and every time they apply for a visa.
When you lodge your application online, you will be sent a request to provide personal identifiers (biometrics) via email. You should make an appointment to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre (ABCC) in person to provide your biometrics. Take a copy of that email and your passport to the appointment.
You must provide your biometrics within 14 days of online lodgement or notify the relevant visa processing office if unable to do so.
VFS Global operates three ABCCs in the Philippines (in Manila, Cebu and Davao city). The ABCC will charge a service fee for the collection of biometrics.
For more information about biometric collection procedures, fees charged, contact details, ABCC locations, or to book your biometrics appointment, please visit Welcome to VFS Global| vfsglobal.
Enquiries
Visa and citizenship applications are managed by the Department of Home Affairs. Embassy staff are unable to assist with general visa or citizenship enquiries.
The Department of Home Affairs website has the most up to date and comprehensive information on applying for visas and citizenship. The website also has useful definitions and tools to help you understand the department’s requirements. Visit the website at Immigration and citizenship.
If you are having trouble locating information on the department’s website, the Home Affairs Digital Assistant may be able to help. The Digital Assistant can help you find information on Australian visas, citizenship and border entry. Visit the Immigration and citizenship website, and click the Ask a question button to get started.
Global Service Centre
If you require additional information, you may telephone the Global Service Centre on +61 2 6196 0196, Monday to Friday, from 9am to 5pm your local time.
International calls may be subject to charges imposed by your local carrier. You may wish to consider using a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) provider to avoid potentially high charges.
Using an interpreter
When you call the GSC, select option 6 to engage a Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS) interpreter in your language. Option 6 can be selected straight after dialling the GSC number.
Alternatively, a TIS interpreter can also be engaged directly via:
TIS website: Search | Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) or
Home Affairs website See: Family and friends helping with your application
Compliments, complaints and suggestions
Your feedback is valuable to the Department of Home Affairs. The department use your feedback to improve services and investigate and respond to any issues of concern. You can find more information on the department’s website at Compliments, complaints and suggestions.
Allegations related to suspicious border activities
​​​​​​​​​​​If it doesn’t feel right, flag it anonymously with Border Watch. Border Watch is the single collection point for the Department of Home Affairs and the Australian Border Force (ABF) for allegations related to suspicious border activities and is not limited to immigration and citizenship. One small observation could help stop a much larger border crime. You can report suspicious immigration, customs and border related activity via the Border Watch Online Report.
Warning regarding visa scams in the Philippines
For information on Stay Safe from Visa Scams, click here.
Changes to Australian citizenship certificates from 1 July 2021
Since 1 July 2021, applicants approved for Australian citizenship by descent and Australian citizenship by adoption will receive an Australian citizenship certificate instead of an Australian citizenship extract. The Government will not issue citizenship extracts for applications approved on or after 1 July 2021. You can still use a citizenship extract (issued prior to 1 July 2021), to apply for an Australian Passport.
Applicants are encouraged to provide an Australian postal address with their application. If you are unable to provide one, we will send your certificate to the Australian Embassy and notify you on how you can collect the certificate. For further information, please visit Evidence of citizenship and certificates.
Contacting the processing office
If you have read this information and still need more information or help, you can contact the visa office at the Australian Embassy in the Philippines here: Australian Immigration Enquiry Form.
